summary.value: The Smith - Lincoln Square is a big, busy American brasserie at 1900 Broadway at 63rd Street, opposite Lincoln Center, open from breakfast to late. Restaurantji diners praise its speed under pressure: one opera-goer said They sat us promptly at our reservation time despite their incredibly busy atmosphere and called the timing impeccable. It suits pre-theater brunch or dinner when you need to make a curtain.

claims.text: They sat us promptly at our reservation time despite their incredibly busy atmosphere

description.value: The Smith - Lincoln Square is an American brasserie at 1900 BROADWAY (AT 63RD STREET). Its posted hours are Mon - Thurs: 8AM - 11PM and later on weekends. It sits right across from Lincoln Center, so it is a handy choice before or after a show. Representative Restaurantji praise (guest reviews): “The seafood tower is quite an experience, treat yourself!”. Representative watch-outs: “their incredibly busy atmosphere”. Restaurantji shows 4 2017 ratings for the 1900 Broadway location. Restaurantji diners add that Brunch at The Smith was an excellent experience, and one writes It tastes good and the environment is very good.

itineraryNote: The Smith - Lincoln Square: a buzzy brasserie at 1900 BROADWAY (AT 63RD STREET) facing Lincoln Center; book before a show and treat yourself to the seafood tower.
review1: The seafood tower is The Smith's signature splurge, with diners recommending it for celebrations and treating it as the dish to share.
review2: Pre-theater timing is a strength, with guests heading to Lincoln Center saying they were seated promptly and served on schedule.
review3: Weekend brunch gets strong reviews, with diners calling it an excellent, satisfying experience that works well for groups. It comes up often enough to plan around.
review4: Expect a busy, loud room, the most common watch-out, so it suits lively meals better than quiet conversation. This pattern shows up across many of the saved reviews.
